rationale_overall: The week's pool is dominated by noise: the Musk-Trump feud over SpaceX/Dragon decommissioning (private company, no ticker), Tesla's Optimus program-lead exit (TSLA not held), Golan rocket fire and Houthi missile intercepts (geopolitical events, not investable securities), foreign/OTC items (BSNL nuclear reactor plans, Niger uranium security, Sukhoi tyre upgrades), and a stream of generic 'AI stock' listicle/prediction pieces with no named catalyst. The one genuine signal is the nuclear/AI-power intersection strengthening further -- Meta's 20-year Constellation Energy (CEG) deal, UBS's bullish NuScale (SMR) note, and a grouped CEG/OKLO/SMR 'powering the AI boom' piece -- which confirms nuclear (SMR near-term) as the next wave building on top of AI, exactly as the profile anticipates. But it is a continuation of an already-known trend rather than a fresh, clearly-stronger-than-a-holding catalyst, and GOOGL/MSFT already carry indirect nuclear-power-for-AI exposure through their own compute buildouts, so no current holding is meaningfully weaker by comparison this week. Per the swap discipline for this cadence, holding the current watchlist unchanged and continuing to track nuclear (SMR/OKLO/CEG) as a watch-list candidate for a future rebalance if the catalyst strengthens or broadens.
